name: PT Suryamas Dutamakmur Tbk

frontmatter.title: Suryamas Dutamakmur — a Bogor land bank priced for a control premium
frontmatter.summary: SMDM owns the Rancamaya estate and two smaller Bogor land banks and is almost wholly controlled by BSDE after the 2025 takeover. The shares trade far above the price the controller itself paid, on a tiny free float, no dividend and earnings too small to carry the multiple. The asset value is book value; the call is the discount, not a growth forecast. We reiterate SELL.
thesis: The controller bought the whole company in 2025 at a price far below today's quote, so the market is paying a premium that minorities cannot monetise.
RNAV is built at carrying value and therefore equals parent book value per share; after the discount it is Rp296, under the traded price.
{'The target is insensitive to our operating forecasts by construction': 'only the RNAV discount moves it, and we say so plainly.'}
{'Earnings do not carry the multiple': 'FY2026E EPS of Rp9 leaves the stock on 46.6x.'}
A free float of 1.0% against a requirement stepping up to 15.0% by 31 March 2029 is an unresolved dilution risk — or, on the mirror route, a cheap buyout.
Cash conversion is poor, dividends are nil and the asset backing is real but only worth book until someone appraises it.

catalysts.event: Annual report and FY2026 results — the first full year of BSDE control and the first clean read on like-for-like revenue
Deadline to meet the free-float requirement, via a placement, a rights issue or a buyout of the minority
Expiry of the VAT exemption on landed houses

blocks.text: We initiate coverage of PT Suryamas Dutamakmur with a **SELL** rating and a twelve-month target of Rp224, -44.2% from the Rp402 last price. The variant view is not that the assets are bad — they are real, carried at historical cost and backed by a controlling shareholder that knows how to develop them. The variant view is that the price already capitalises a control premium that a minority holder cannot reach, while the cash flows, the float and the dividend record all point the other way. Our blended value is Rp286 per share before the liquidity haircut, and the RNAV leg — the one that matters for a land company — is Rp296 after a discount of 40.0% and the separate liquidity haircut [S0] [S3].

This revision answers the first red-team pass and changes three things of substance. First, we no longer claim the development margin or the cap rate drive the target: they do not. The RNAV leg carries the majority of the weight, it is built from the balance sheet, and the earnings and book cross-checks are struck off reported last-twelve-month earnings and current equity, so no operating forecast in this engine reaches the target at all. The number that matters is the discount, and the effective one is 40.0% compounded with the 30.0% liquidity haircut. Second, we state that the pre-discount RNAV equals parent book value per share almost exactly — it is an identity at carrying value, not an independent estimate — and that no sourced land appraisal exists to mark it up. Third, the reverse test the extreme-call gate asks for cannot be bracketed on growth, and we now say what that means rather than asserting a result the model does not produce.

SMDM is a Bogor-focused developer. It owns the Rancamaya Golf Estate, a mature 400 ha township with a golf course, hotel, clubhouse and remaining land, the Tajur Boulevard site of 7.2 ha in Tajur's central business district, and Harvest City in Cileungsi through its subsidiaries [S16] [S3]. Revenue is overwhelmingly development sales — 260 IDR bn in FY2025A — with hotel, rental and estate services making up the rest [S9]. The company was established in September 1989 and listed in October 1995 [S2], and was, until the 2025 takeover, controlled by Top Global Limited, which the filing treats as a third party to BSDE rather than a related party [S3]; BSDE now holds 99.0% of the shares and consolidates SMDM into the Sinar Mas Land group [S3].

The price is the problem, and much of the move has already happened. The pack puts the trading range over the last twelve months at Rp368 to Rp1,260, against Rp402 today and a market value of IDR1,918.4bn, so the shares have given back most of their run and sit near the low rather than at a fresh high [S0]. We are not arguing against a speculative spike; we are arguing that even after that de-rating the price exceeds the only arm's-length whole-company price by a wide margin, and that the remaining gap needs a named event to close. BSDE paid 1,196 IDR bn for 4,390 m shares in a transaction settled in September 2025 — the only price for control that exists [S3] — and the shares now change hands at Rp402 on a free float of 1.0% and insider ownership of 99.0% [S0]. A stock with a float that thin is not priced by marginal sellers; it is priced by scarcity, and scarcity is not a fundamental.

The cross-checks diverge, and the divergence is informative rather than a problem. The RNAV leg says Rp296, the own-history price/earnings leg says Rp92 and the price/book leg says Rp450 [S0]. The book leg is the highest because the shares trade below book — 0.8x on our FY2026E equity — while the earnings leg is the lowest because earnings collapsed in FY2025 and only partly recover in our forecasts. For a company whose value sits in land rather than in its P&L, the asset leg should dominate, which is why it carries the largest weight. Both cross-checks are explained in section four rather than smoothed away.

What would change our mind: a disclosed plan to release land at appraised rather than carrying value, a real free-float increase that brings in price-setting investors, or a dividend policy that returns the growing cash balance. None of those is announced. Until one is, the most probable path is a share price that drifts back toward the value of the assets it represents.

SMDM's business is the development and sale of land and landed houses in Greater Jakarta's southern fringe, plus the operation of the estate infrastructure that makes that land saleable. Rancamaya, in Bogor, is the core: a golf estate opened in the early years of the company's life, with a hotel, a clubhouse and a remaining land bank that the group reports at carrying cost [S16] [S3]. Tajur Boulevard and Harvest City are smaller, earlier-stage projects in the same corridor, and the group also holds strata-title units and rental property that generate a modest recurring stream [S9].

The segment mix is narrow and has become narrower. In FY2025A land, houses and shophouses produced 260 IDR bn of revenue, the hotel 52.5 IDR bn, strata-title sales 3.8 IDR bn, other segments 66.6 IDR bn and rental 2.9 IDR bn [S9]. Development is therefore roughly two-thirds of the top line even in a year when it fell by almost half, and it drives essentially all of the gross profit. The model in this report builds revenue from the development line plus the other-segments bucket; the hotel, strata-title and rental lines are disclosed separately by the company and are not inside the revenue build. We no longer describe that as a rounding difference: it is a scope choice with a stated cost, set out in section three, and it makes our forecast revenue and EBITDA conservative relative to the reported total [S9].

The strategy under BSDE control is continuity rather than reinvention. The acquirer's stated intent is to continue developing Tajur and Harvest City and to add premium housing, hotel capacity, a golf course and villas at Rancamaya [S16]. That is a land-release strategy funded from the balance sheet rather than a new-build strategy funded from debt, and it fits a company that sits on net cash and has no borrowing programme [S0]. The group's own disclosures show the controlling shareholder running a much larger township business — BSDE booked group marketing sales of IDR10.04tn in FY2025 [S8] — so the operational playbook exists inside the parent even if SMDM's own release pace is slow.

Competitively, SMDM is a challenger in a fragmented market and a price-taker on land. Its position rests on a finite, well-located land bank in a corridor where supply of titled land with infrastructure is constrained, and on the golf estate's brand within Bogor [S16]. It does not have the scale, the land pipeline or the buyer franchise of the large listed developers, and it has no control over mortgage rates or the subsidy and tax regime that determine affordability. The moat is the land itself and the entitlements attached to it — real, but not a moat that lets the company set prices.

The corporate structure matters more than the operating story. SMDM is a holding company over project subsidiaries in which it does not own everything: minority interests absorbed IDR959.0bn of balance-sheet equity at the end of FY2025A, close to a third of the group total [S0]. Value that accrues at the project level therefore does not all accrue to SMDM shareholders, and any RNAV work has to subtract the minority claim before it divides by the share count. We do that explicitly, and it is one of the reasons our asset value per share is well below the headline land numbers.

Indonesian property development is a rate-sensitive, credit-driven business, and the macro setting in 2026 is supportive at the margin but not stimulative. Bank Indonesia held its policy rate at 5.75 percent in October 2026 [S10], the easing cycle having stalled rather than reversed, and mortgage rates follow the policy rate with a lag. The government has extended the hundred-percent VAT exemption on landed houses to the end of 2027 [S11], which pulls demand forward but also sets up a cliff: buyers who can wait until the exemption lapses have no incentive to transact early, and developers know it. The third quarter of 2026 showed listed developers' revenue recovering from a weak base rather than entering a boom [S4].

The demand pool SMDM sells into is Bogor and the southern Jakarta fringe — aspirational landed housing for middle-income buyers who commute or work locally. That segment is the most mortgage-dependent part of the market and the most exposed to the subsidy and tax regime. It is also where land prices have the longest history of appreciation, which is why carrying-cost land banks understate value; but the gap between carrying cost and market value only becomes cash when the land is released, and release is paced by infrastructure, permits and demand rather than by the balance sheet [S16]. A land bank is an option, and options are worth what the market will pay for them today.

Competitive positioning is best described as regional and sub-scale. The large listed developers compete on land pipeline, brand and access to construction credit; SMDM competes on a single established estate and on the patience of a controlling shareholder that can fund infrastructure without leverage [S3] [S16]. The five forces are unfavourable on the supply side — land owners and contractors hold pricing power, and entitlement risk sits with the developer — and only moderately better on the demand side, where switching costs are low and buyers compare on price, location and financing. The one genuinely defensible asset is the entitled, serviced land inside Rancamaya, which cannot be replicated quickly.

Regulation cuts both ways. The VAT exemption supports volumes until it lapses [S11]; the exchange's high-share-concentration regime, expanded to 383 names in November 2026, imposes a special trading mechanism on issuers on the list and requires a documented improvement in public distribution before an issuer can leave it [S13] [S12]. SMDM's ownership profile — insider holding near the whole company and a free float barely above one percent [S0] — is the shape the regime is aimed at, but we must be precise about what we can and cannot confirm: the published list in [S14] does not name SMDM, we hold no source for its board or notation status, and we therefore withdraw the earlier implication that it sits on the list. What is verifiable is the economics: a float this thin with a traded value of IDR30.6m a day makes any exit of size expensive, list membership or not.

The controlling shareholder's own market is the best guide to what is achievable. BSDE's group marketing sales of IDR10.04tn in FY2025 and its stated plan to keep developing Tajur and Harvest City show that the parent can sell Bogor land at scale [S8] [S16]. The constraint on SMDM is not demand at the group level; it is the pace at which a company with a very small public float and no dividend chooses to release its inventory. That is a governance variable, and we treat it as one.

Indonesian landed-housing developers have historically created value by holding entitled land through
cycles and releasing it slowly, which means reported earnings lag land-price inflation by years and
book value understates replacement cost. The market has typically resolved that gap with a discount
rather than a premium, because minority holders cannot force a sale of the land bank and the
controlling family sets the release schedule. That pattern is the lens we apply here.

The reported history is a collapse and a modest recovery. Revenue fell from IDR694.0bn in FY2024A to IDR386.1bn in FY2025A, with net profit to the parent dropping from IDR123.8bn to IDR22.1bn over the same two years [S0] [S9]. Gross margin held up — 62.9% in FY2025A — because the cost of revenue fell with the revenue, but operating costs did not: SG&A absorbed 50.0% of revenue in our first forecast year after IDR202.9bn of cost on a depressed base in FY2025A [S0]. That is the operating leverage story in one line: the estate's cost base is largely fixed, so a recovering top line converts into EBITDA quickly, and a falling one destroys margin.

Our forecast is a recovery in the nine-month run-rate, not a recovery in the full-year level, and the distinction matters. Development revenue grows 30.0% in FY2026E — the template's ceiling — because the nine-month run-rate is up by roughly two-fifths year on year while the exceptional fourth quarter of FY2025A is not repeated in full [S0]. But the build carries only the development line and the other-segments bucket, so modelled revenue of IDR408.5bn is 5.8% above the reported FY2025A total of 386 IDR bn — a mid-single-digit year, and it implies a fourth quarter below the prior year's. The three lines outside the build are the hotel at 52.5 IDR bn, strata-title sales at 3.8 IDR bn and rent at 2.9 IDR bn [S9]. At the recurring margin of 50.0% their gross profit is a material share of the IDR58.6bn EBITDA we forecast, so modelled EBITDA is conservative by roughly that amount. We state the gap rather than netting it away because it is the largest single reconciliation between our model and the reported accounts; a reader who grosses the model up should see a higher EBITDA and an unchanged target, because the RNAV does not read the P&L. The omission is mechanical, not a forecast that those segments vanish: the engine's property template carries a development line and a single recurring bucket, and the three reported lines sit outside it. They are disclosed here with their own sources so the reconciliation can be made line by line against the reported total of 386 IDR bn. No earnings-based valuation leg is ever struck off the reduced build — both cross-checks use reported trailing earnings and reported equity — so the omission affects the forecast and the margin commentary, never the target.

Growth then fades to high single digits as Rancamaya, Royal Tajur and Harvest City release on their existing plans with no new land acquisition disclosed [S16]. Revenue reaches IDR452.6bn in FY2027E and IDR538.4bn by FY2030E, with EBITDA of IDR72.7bn and IDR103.6bn respectively. Margins stay near the FY2025A level: development gross margin of 65.5% fading half a point a year as later, higher-cost phases are released, and recurring margin of 50.0% [S9].

Two features of the model deserve to be stated plainly because they are the weakest links. First, the presales driver is development revenue, not marketing sales: SMDM does not publish a presales KPI, and we have not been able to obtain its annual report or quarterly filings directly, so the recognition lag is set to zero and the driver is the recognised line [S9]. That reproduces reported revenue exactly but removes the lead indicator a property analyst would normally use. Second, the revenue build excludes the hotel, strata-title and rental segments as set out above, and the FY2026E revenue and margin figures should be read as like-for-like on that narrower base [S9].

Cash generation is the earnings-quality flag, and it is where the screen pays for itself. Operating cash flow was negative in both of the last two fiscal years while net profit was positive, which puts the accruals ratio — net profit less operating cash flow, over average total assets — at a low single-digit percentage rather than the double-digit level that would make the margins suspect [S0]. The divergence sits in inventory, not receivables: cost of revenue fell from IDR298.5bn to IDR143.2bn while inventory rose, so inventory now stands at a multiple of revenue [S0]. For a land developer that is the ordinary shape of the business — finished stock and land awaiting release — but it is a real gap between reported profit and cash, and it is why free cash flow to the firm was IDR-1.6bn [S0]. The working-capital ratio to revenue in our model is 1.4x, close to the three-year average but below the FY2025A ratio, which was inflated by the collapsed revenue denominator [S0].

The balance sheet is the strongest part of the case. SMDM is in net cash — cash of IDR151.8bn against debt of IDR30.8bn at the end of FY2025A, a net cash position of IDR-121.0bn on the model's sign convention [S0] — and parent equity of IDR2,303.3bn sits against total assets of 3,530 IDR bn [S9]. Capital expenditure is small at 2.5% of revenue, because land acquisition sits in inventory rather than in capex, and there is no borrowing programme [S0]. The weakness is on the other side of the ledger: minority interests of IDR959.0bn absorb a large share of consolidated equity, so the parent's claim on the assets is materially smaller than the group numbers suggest.

One data caveat, because it bears on every asset number we use. The subsidiary table in BSDE's consolidated filing reports SMDM's total assets on a before-eliminations basis materially above the total-assets figure our data pack carries for the same date [S3] [S0], and we could not reconcile the two without SMDM's own consolidated accounts, which we could not obtain. We use the pack consistently for history, equity, minority and the RNAV inputs rather than mixing sources; if SMDM's own accounts show the larger balance sheet, our asset base is too small and our case too conservative, which is a direction we would rather flag than hide.

Capital allocation has been passive. No dividend was paid in any year of the pack's history, the payout ratio we model is 0.0%, and the cash balance has been allowed to build rather than being returned or redeployed [S0]. Under BSDE control the incentive to distribute is weaker still: the parent owns almost everything, so a dividend would be a transfer from one pocket to another, while a minority holder receives nothing. Return on equity reflects it — 1.8% in FY2026E on our numbers, well below the cost of equity — and that is the arithmetic behind the earnings-based valuation leg being so much lower than the asset-based one.

We value SMDM on RNAV as the primary method, with price/earnings and price/book as cross-checks. That set fits the industry: the company's value is its entitled land and the infrastructure around it, not its current earnings, and a discounted-cash-flow model would capitalise a release schedule we cannot observe. The weights are those the house applies to Indonesian developers — RNAV carrying the majority, earnings and book splitting the rest — and we have not changed them [S0]. The RNAV is built from the balance sheet because no appraisal exists: SMDM reports its land at carrying cost, and the Rancamaya land for development alone is 1,355,548 sqm carried at 576 IDR bn [S3]. Ready-for-sale Rancamaya inventory is 1,106 IDR bn, Harvest City 69.9 IDR bn and Royal Tajur 69.5 IDR bn [S3].

The cost of equity is built as the risk-free rate of 7.4% less the 1.6% Indonesian sovereign default spread, plus a levered beta of 0.91 multiplied by the sum of the 4.2% mature-market equity risk premium and the 2.5% country risk premium, which gives a cost of equity of 11.9% [S0]. Read as arithmetic, the net risk-free leg is 7.4% − 1.6% and the equity-risk leg is 0.91 × (4.2% + 2.5%); the levered beta is the unlevered 0.90 re-geared at the 22.0% tax rate on the small debt weight, which is the whole of the re-gearing. That is why the stated 11.9% is below the sum of its headline components: the sovereign spread is subtracted, not added. The WACC is 11.9% at a debt weight of 1.6% [S0]. The near-zero debt weight is the consequence of the net cash position, which is why WACC and cost of equity are almost the same number. We roll the value forward at the cost of equity and then apply the liquidity haircut the house requires for a stock this illiquid: average daily traded value is IDR30.6m, far below the threshold at which no haircut applies, so 30.0% comes off the value [S0].

The RNAV leg is a book-value measure and we should say so without dressing it up. The land bank input is total assets at 30 September 2026 less cash, less the non-debt liabilities that fund the asset base and less the recurring business the engine capitalises separately; the line-by-line build is in the assumption file and it nets to the carrying value of the property inventory and estate assets. Adding the capitalised recurring stream back (at the 18.0% rate applied to recurring gross profit), deducting net debt and the full minority interest and dividing by the share count returns an RNAV per share within a fraction of a percent of parent book value per share at the same date [S0] [S3]. The RNAV is Rp296 after the discount; the pre-discount figure is parent book by construction, not because two independent estimates happen to agree. That matters for how the leg should be read: it is not evidence about what the land is worth, and the only thing that could make it evidence is an appraisal, which we do not have.

No sourced land uplift exists in this file. We could not obtain SMDM's annual report or quarterly filings, the company reports land at carrying cost, and we found no published Bogor corridor land benchmark, NJOP schedule or appraisal we could cite without inventing a number. The red team's own arithmetic shows what is at stake — a mark-up of Rancamaya land above carrying cost is worth a double-digit percentage of the target per rupiah of land value — and we would rather state that the asset case rests on book than import a land price from a broker note, which the house quarantines. The one arm's-length whole-company price that does exist points the other way: BSDE paid 1,196 IDR bn for 4,390 m shares in 2025 [S3], a price below book, and today's Rp402 is a premium to it.

The discount is the assumption, so we state the one actually applied. A 40.0% RNAV discount and a 30.0% liquidity haircut compound: the asset leg reaches the target at roughly two-fifths of RNAV and, since RNAV equals book, at roughly two-fifths of book. With the earnings and book legs in the blend the target is Rp224 against a book value per share of Rp491, under half of book. We do not claim that discount is out of line with the listed developer peer set: on this desk's own models LPCK and LPKR are carried well below book too, so the peer comparison cuts both ways and we rest the case on the control price, not on relative P/B. We no longer run the argument that a second discount would double count — the model contradicts it, and so would a reader. The reason the discount is defensible is narrower and empirical: the only arm's-length control price was struck below book, the float cannot be exited at size, and no appraisal exists. If a reader rejects that anchor, the discount is the whole of the call and the shares are a hold; we would rather put that choice in front of the reader than bury it in a blend. That resolves the apparent contradiction between a target below the control price and a control price below today's quote: the IDR1,196.4bn BSDE paid for the controlling block [S3] carried no minority exit discount and no float constraint, while the 30.0% haircut is precisely the cost a float of 1.0% imposes on the exit. A reader who rejects the haircut should work from Rp286, the blend before it — still below today's Rp402, so the rating survives the objection, but the distance is the haircut, not the asset analysis.

The cross-checks diverge in opposite directions and both are explained. The P/E cross-check gives Rp92, -69.0% against the primary method, because the own-history mean multiple of 11.5x is struck not against our forecast but against reported trailing parent earnings at 30 September 2026, which are lower than the FY2026E recovery we forecast — a depressed base, and a land developer's earnings are a poor measure of its asset value [S0] [S3]. Our FY2026E EPS of Rp9 is the forecast that the leg deliberately does not use; on that higher base the multiple would give a larger cross-check, but we keep the engine's reported-earnings basis so the two cross-checks are struck on a consistent, audited-quality number rather than on our own forecast [S0]. The P/BV cross-check gives Rp450, 52.1% against the primary, because the shares change hands at 0.8x book and the own-history mean of 0.9x book assumes a re-rating toward the level the stock has traded at historically [S0]. We keep both at their house weights rather than hand-adjusting them, and we flag the divergence here rather than hiding it in a blend.

The sensitivity table is generated from the industry template and it tells a narrower story than the round-one text claimed. Both axes are shocked across symmetric steps, and the columns along the presales-growth axis are identical to the last decimal: the target is completely invariant to presales growth, because the RNAV leg carries the majority of the weight and is a balance-sheet calculation, while the earnings and book legs are struck off reported last-twelve-month earnings and current equity and so do not read the forecast at all. What moves the answer is the other axis. A twenty-point swing in the RNAV discount takes the target between Rp284 and Rp357 — within a few rupiah of the corresponding bear and bull scenario values, the small difference being the recurring-margin shock, which reaches the value only through the recurring leg. The discount is the only shock common to both the grid and the scenarios that moves the number materially. Repeating the grid on the development gross margin produces a flat column for the same reason; repeating it on the cap rate, or on the recurring margin, tilts the target only through the recurring leg, which is a small share of RNAV — the table's cap-rate block shows the tilt is a few rupiah a share, not tens. The honest statement of the method is therefore: the rating is a discount and liquidity call, the operating forecasts describe the business but do not set the target, and a reader who disagrees with the discount disagrees with the rating rather than with the model.

What today's price implies is not a growth rate, and we will not pretend it is. The engine's reverse test — solve for the presales growth that makes the primary method equal the price — returns no solution and records the price as not bracketed, because the RNAV leg contains no growth term and nothing the test can vary lifts the RNAV value of Rp296 to Rp402. That failure is the finding: no presales growth in any range makes the asset leg worth the price, so the price is not a growth forecast. At Rp402 the market pays 0.8x book and 46.6x our FY2026E earnings — a book multiple above our target's and an earnings multiple that requires either an appraisal uplift we cannot source or a control event minorities cannot force. Neither is in the base case.

The downside risks we weigh most heavily are structural rather than cyclical. Ownership concentration is the first: with insider holding at 99.0% and a free float of 1.0%, the shares are a scarcity asset, and scarcity can persist in both directions — it supports the price on the way up and makes exit expensive on the way down [S0]. The free-float requirement of 15.0% by 31 March 2029 is the second, and it has two directions rather than one [S15]. The bear route is a discounted placement or a rights issue, which transfers value from existing minorities. The bull route, which round one omitted, is a buyout: with a float of barely one percent, buying the minority out at an appraised price would cost BSDE a fraction of the 1,196 IDR bn it paid for control, and a delisting buyback would require exactly the independent appraisal this report says would change our mind. We put that route in the bull case because ignoring it is a one-sided reading. It does not rescue the rating: even at full RNAV, before any discount, the asset leg after the liquidity haircut still sits below today's Rp402, so a buyout at book protects minorities without paying today's price. Only an appraisal above book closes the gap, and that is the unsourced input again. The buyout is deliberately outside the probability-weighted scenario set: the float deadline is 31 March 2029, past our twelve-month horizon, so we name the route and describe its value rather than fold a multi-year event into a one-year target. If the deadline were pulled forward, the bull case would have to carry it with its own probability, and the weighted value would rise toward the pre-liquidity blend.

The operating risks are the ordinary ones for a land developer. Demand depends on mortgage rates and on a VAT exemption that lapses at the end of 2027 [S11]; a policy cliff in a market where the central bank has stopped cutting at 5.75 percent [S10] is a real risk to the release schedule. Land release is paced by permits and infrastructure, and delay pushes revenue out without reducing the fixed cost base. Commodity and FX exposure is minimal because the business is domestic and rupiah-denominated, and liquidity risk is low at the company level — net cash, no maturity wall — even though it is severe at the shareholder level, where the traded value is a few tens of millions of rupiah a day [S0].

Governance and related-party risk deserve their own line, and the first duty is to separate what we can source from what we cannot. BSDE controls 99.0% of SMDM and consolidates it into the Sinar Mas Land group [S3]; that is a fact. The round-one claim that the controller is also SMDM's main contractor, its infrastructure provider and a potential buyer of its land was inference, not disclosure, and we withdraw it as stated. We could not obtain SMDM's own related-party note, and the related-party balances in the consolidated filing are BSDE's rather than SMDM's [S3], so the house screen's related-party share of revenue cannot be computed from what we hold: we record it as not verified rather than as zero. What we can say is that the valuation does not depend on the answer in one direction. The base case already values the entire land bank at carrying cost and never assumes a market-value release, so a controller who releases land at cost cannot erode an asset value that never credited an uplift in the first place. The leakage we fear is not in the RNAV; it is in the price, which already assumes an uplift no minority can force.

Our scenarios mirror the same drivers in both directions. The bear case takes development growth down by ten percentage points from the 30.0% base path, compresses the recurring gross margin by the same ten points and widens the RNAV discount by ten points, reflecting a demand cliff when the VAT exemption lapses and a discounted placement to fix the float; the bull case takes each up by the same amount and narrows the discount, reflecting a rate-cut-driven recovery and a re-rating toward appraised land value, with the buyout as the corporate route to the same end. Probabilities are 50.0% base, 25.0% bear and 25.0% bull. The arithmetic the round-one text got wrong is now stated: the growth and margin shocks change the forecast but reach the target only through the recurring leg, so almost all of the Rp284 to Rp357 spread is the discount, and even the bull case leaves the shares below today's price once the liquidity haircut is applied. The signposts that would change the view are a disclosed appraisal, an announced float mechanism — placement, rights issue or buyout — that brings in price-setting investors, a dividend policy, and a sustained recovery in development revenue above our forecast.

SMDM is a controlled company in the fullest sense. BSDE holds 99.0% of the shares after buying 4,390 m shares from Top Global Limited for 1,196 IDR bn in a transaction settled in September 2025, and consolidates SMDM into the Sinar Mas Land group [S3]. The remaining float is 1.0%, with institutions at 0.0% [S0]. That structure explains most of the governance profile: minority shareholders have no practical ability to block related-party transactions, to force a land sale or to change the board, and the controlling shareholder's interests are pursued at the group level rather than at SMDM's.

The exchange's regime now flags this shape of company, but not this company on the evidence we hold. The high-share-concentration list was expanded to 383 names in November 2026, and the exchange requires issuers seeking to leave it to demonstrate improved public distribution through real trades in the regular market [S13] [S12]. We checked the published list [S14]: it does not name SMDM, and no source we hold states the board or notation status of the issuer. We therefore withdraw the earlier implication that SMDM sits on the special list and record the status as unverified — the liquidity haircut in the valuation rests on the IDR30.6m traded value and the 1.0% float [S0], not on a board designation. The free-float deadline of 31 March 2029 applies to issuers below the size threshold, which SMDM is [S15]. We treat the absence of an announced plan as a governance gap rather than as comfort, and we would resolve the board question with the company's own filings the moment we can obtain them.

On the disclosure we can check, we must be careful about what we claim. Round one said there was no restatement, no going-concern notation and no manipulation-class flag; that was inference from a data pack, not an audit opinion, and we could not obtain SMDM's annual report to verify the opinion, the related-party note or the absence of notations. We downgrade the claim to not verified and rest the earnings-quality read on what the numbers themselves show: operating cash flow negative in both of the last two fiscal years against positive net profit, an accruals ratio in low single digits on our calculation from the pack rather than the double-digit level that would imply margins outrunning cash, and inventory rising while cost of revenue fell from IDR298.5bn to IDR143.2bn [S0]. That is an optics-class pattern for a land developer, not a manipulation-class one, and the test that would settle it — the audited accounts — is a document we do not have.

The dividend record is the weak point. Nil in every year of the pack's history, with the payout ratio modelled at 0.0% [S0]. A controlling shareholder that neither pays out nor sells land is asking minorities to wait indefinitely, and the market's premium to our value is not compensation for that wait.

ESG exposure is modest but not zero. The business is land development in a water-stressed corridor, which brings drainage, flood and community-relations risk at the project level; the golf course is a water-intensive asset with a reputational dimension. Social and governance factors dominate the assessment, and the governance factor is the one that matters for valuation: a company that is almost entirely owned by another listed company will be run for the group, and minorities should price that accordingly [S3].

The dated catalysts are the annual report and FY2026 results, which will show whether the nine-month recovery holds at the full-year level and whether BSDE begins to accelerate land release [S9]; the lapse of the hundred-percent VAT exemption at the end of 2027, which is the clearest test of underlying demand [S11]; and the 31 March 2029 free-float deadline, which will eventually force a capital-structure decision — placement, rights issue or buyout [S15]. We also watch any announcement of a land appraisal or a related-party land sale, because either would give the market a price for assets that are currently carried at cost, and that is the single event that would move us off this rating [S3].

The operating KPIs we monitor are development revenue and its split between Rancamaya, Royal Tajur and Harvest City; the gross margin on released phases; the pace of inventory release against the 1,355,548 sqm of Rancamaya land for development [S3]; and the cash balance, which is the only source of dividend capacity in a company with no borrowing programme [S0]. On the governance side we watch the free float, the traded value, any placement or rights issue, any change in the composition of the board or the audit arrangements, and any change in SMDM's board or notation status at the exchange — that last one we have flagged as unverified and will resolve when the company's own filings are available. A move in any of those would be more informative than the quarterly earnings print, because the earnings print does not reach the valuation: with the asset leg at book and both cross-checks on reported figures, what the share price is paying for is the appraisal or control event nobody has announced.

bear.narrative: Property demand stays weak after the VAT exemption lapses at end-2027 (F35), Rancamaya releases slow, revenue falls instead of recovering, hotel and estate-services margins compress with occupancy, and the controlling shareholder fixes the 1% free float with a discounted placement that dilutes minorities.

bull.narrative: Rate cuts and the VAT exemption to end-2027 lift Bogor landed-house demand, Rancamaya and Harvest City releases sell at better prices, revenue compounds in the mid-teens, hotel and estate-services margins recover, and the market re-rates the land bank toward appraised rather than carrying value. The mirror route to the same end is a buyout: with a float of barely one percent, buying the minority out at an appraised price would cost BSDE a tiny fraction of what it paid for control, and the appraisal itself would be the first independent land mark.

sensitivity.title: 12-month value vs presales growth and RNAV discount

assumptions.label: Presales growth
assumptions.basis: The driver is development revenue (SMDM discloses no marketing-sales KPI), so growth is read off the reported revenue run-rate: 9M 2026 revenue was Rp280.8bn against Rp200.4bn in 9M 2025 (+40% YoY, S0 quarterly), while Q4 2025 alone was Rp185.7bn and is not repeated in full. FY2026E is therefore set at the template's 30% ceiling, then normalises to high single digits on a flat Rancamaya/Royal Tajur/Harvest City release plan with no new land acquisition disclosed. Scope note for the reader: the build carries only the development and other-segments lines (Rp260.4bn + Rp66.6bn = Rp327.0bn of the Rp386.1bn reported in FY2025A); the hotel, strata-title and rental lines (Rp52.5bn, Rp3.8bn, Rp2.9bn, F4/F5/F6) are outside it because the template has one development and one recurring line. So 30% development growth lifts modelled revenue to Rp408.5bn, which is 5.8% on the reported total (fin.FY2026E.revenue_growth) and implies Q4 2026 below Q4 2025 — a like-for-like mid-single-digit year, not a 30% recovery, and the level of modelled revenue is 15.4% below reported. Modelled EBITDA is conservative by the gross profit on the three omitted lines at the recurring margin. The driver also does not move the target at all: the RNAV leg is a balance-sheet measure and the earnings and book legs are struck off reported LTM earnings and current equity, so presales growth changes the forecast, not the value (see the sensitivity grid and report section 4).

assumptions.label: Share of presales recognised in the same year
assumptions.basis: Set to 1.0 because the driver series is already recognised development revenue, not marketing sales (SMDM publishes no presales figure). With recog_current = 1 the model reproduces reported revenue exactly in the base year and the recognition lag is not double counted; the cost is that a genuine presales lead indicator is absent, which is flagged in the report.

assumptions.label: Recurring revenue growth
assumptions.basis: Recurring bucket is the other-segments line (Rp66.6bn FY2025, F3) — hotel, rental and services are reported separately and are not in the revenue build. Growth follows occupancy and tariff on a fixed asset base (no new hotel or mall rooms disclosed), with the BI rate cutting cycle (5.75%, S10) a mild support; terminal at Indonesian long-run inflation.

assumptions.label: Development gross margin
assumptions.basis: Blended FY2025 gross margin was 62.9% (gross profit Rp242.88bn on revenue Rp386.08bn, F13/F7); SMDM does not split segment cost of sales, so the development line is set marginally above the blend at 65.5% — Rancamaya land and landed houses carry the highest margin, hotel and services the lowest — and fades 0.5pp a year as later, higher-cost phases at Harvest City and Royal Tajur are released. No erosion assumed beyond that.

assumptions.label: Recurring gross margin
assumptions.basis: Other-segments revenue is a mix of hotel/estate services and miscellaneous income rather than a pure rental stream, so it is set at 50% — below the group blend of 62.9% (F13/F7) because the services component carries staff costs in cost of revenue — rising 0.5pp a year with operating leverage on a fixed cost base.

assumptions.label: Cap rate for investment property (RNAV)
assumptions.basis: Applied to recurring gross profit as a proxy for NOI: a 9% NOI cap rate for Bogor hotel and rental assets divided by a ~50% NOI-to-gross-profit ratio (opex and maintenance take about half of the 50% recurring margin), giving 0.18. Cross-checked against the carrying value of the hotel and estate assets inside the landbank_value, which the capitalised figure broadly matches.

assumptions.label: Target discount to RNAV
assumptions.basis: 40%, the narrow end of the 40-70% band the house applies to Indonesian developers on the RNAV leg, but not the discount the reader actually gets. The engine then removes a separate 30% liquidity haircut for a Rp30.6m ADTV, and the two compound: the asset leg reaches the target at 0.6 x 0.7 = 0.42 of RNAV, an effective 58% discount, and because our RNAV equals parent book value per share (see landbank_basis) that is 0.42x book. With the earnings and book legs in the blend the target lands at 0.48x book, below the 0.55-0.72x book at which this desk carries the listed developer peer set and at the bottom of the house band. We state 58% as the assumption in the report. It is defensible here only because the one arm's-length whole-company price — BSDE's 2025 purchase of 91.99% at Rp1,196.4bn (F22/F23) — was struck below book, not above it; if a reader rejects that anchor, the discount is the whole of the SELL and the shares are a hold.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025A operating expense was Rp202.9bn (gross profit Rp242.88bn less EBIT Rp39.96bn, S0) or 52.6% of revenue because the revenue base collapsed 44% (F8). Costs are held broadly flat in real terms as revenue recovers, so the ratio falls from 50% to 44% by FY2030E rather than staying at the peak ratio.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025A depreciation of Rp5.81bn on revenue of Rp386.08bn (S0), i.e. 1.5%, versus the 0.96% three-year average — the FY2025 charge is used because it reflects the current asset base (hotel, golf course, estate infrastructure) and the pack's D&A is the only available figure (SMDM's LK could not be obtained to check the cash-flow-method understatement flagged in the desk file).

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025A capex of Rp11.47bn on revenue of Rp386.08bn (2.97%, S0) against a 1.58% three-year average; 2.5% is used — above the average because estate infrastructure and the golf course need upkeep, below the FY2025 spike. Development land acquisition is inside inventory and the working-capital line, not capex.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: Three-year average of 1.44x revenue from the pack (S0), which is inventory-heavy in a normal way for a land developer; the FY2025A ratio of 1.93x is inflated by the collapsed revenue denominator. Used for the DCF cross-check only — RNAV is the primary method and does not depend on it.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: Ten per cent, the pack's three-year average effective rate (S0). A developer pays final income tax of 2.5% on gross property revenue plus normal tax on non-property income, which is why the group rate sits far below the statutory 22%.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: Pack three-year average of 11.0% (S0); interest expense was Rp12.79bn in FY2025 on a small debt balance (Rp30.76bn), so the implied rate is distorted by fees and lease interest and the line is immaterial to value — net cash is positive (Rp188.8bn cash at 30 Sep 2026).

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: Pack three-year average of 3.8% (S0); FY2025 interest income was Rp9.95bn on opening cash of Rp276.1bn (F20). Indonesian time-deposit rates at a 5.75% policy rate support at least this level, so the default is not optimistic.

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: Zero. SMDM is in net cash (cash Rp188.8bn versus debt Rp30.8bn at 30 Sep 2026, S0) and has no disclosed borrowing programme; the controlling shareholder funded the 2025 acquisition at its own level, not at SMDM's.

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: Zero, because no recurring non-operating item is disclosed; FY2025 net profit already includes the estate's interest income and there is no reported one-off to annualise.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: FY2025A minorities took Rp4.44bn of Rp26.55bn net profit (S0), i.e. 16.7%, higher than the 11.2% three-year average because the profitable entity mix shifted; 16.7% is used and it matters only for the PE cross-check, since the RNAV subtracts the full minority balance-sheet interest (Rp928.4bn at 30 Sep 2026).

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: Zero. DPS was nil in FY2023-FY2025 in the pack (S0) and no dividend policy is disclosed; SMDM has never been a dividend payer at this level of earnings and the controlling shareholder takes value through control of the land bank instead.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: Zero in the base case. The one structural risk that could change it is the 15% free-float requirement with a 31 March 2029 deadline (S15), which could be met by a placement or rights issue; that is a bear-case item, not the base case, because no plan has been announced.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: 4% nominal, in line with the house long-run Indonesian nominal growth assumption and with land-price inflation in Greater Jakarta/Bogor; used only for the DCF cross-check.

challenges.challenge: The sensitivity and scenario analysis described in the report is not the one the model runs. The sensitivities grid is constant along the presales-growth axis (353.10 / 336.54 / 319.98 / 303.42 / 286.86 for every one of the five growth steps), so the target is invariant to every operating driver and the whole 287-353 scenario range comes from plus or minus 10pp on a.rnav_discount alone. Section 4 nonetheless tells the reader that the RNAV discount and the development gross margin dominate, the cap rate matters less and the terminal growth rate matters least - three drivers the table never varies - and section 5 says the bear takes development growth down by 30.0% where the shock is -10pp (30% to 20%) and the bull +10pp (40%). A reader cannot test the rating from the document.
challenges.answer: Sections 4 and 5 rewritten. The grid is flat along presales growth because the RNAV leg carries 60% of the weight and is a balance-sheet calculation while the earnings and book legs are struck off reported LTM earnings and current equity: no operating driver reaches the target in this engine. The text now says only the RNAV discount moves it, quotes the bear-to-bull span from the scenario values, and states that dev margin is flat and cap rate tilts it only through the recurring leg [S0].

challenges.challenge: The extreme_call BLOCK was cleared with a statement that is not true. The justification says the reverse DCF in the report states what growth the price implies, but fund record records reverse_dcf as available=false with note price not bracketed, and section 4 contains no reverse DCF - only 46.6x FY2026E earnings and 0.83x book. The gate exists precisely to force the implied-growth test on a -44% call and it has not been performed.
challenges.answer: The reverse test returns available=false, target a.presales_growth, note price not bracketed, and section 4 now states that plainly: no presales growth in any range lifts the RNAV value to the price because the leg has no growth term, so the price is not a growth forecast. The extreme_call justification was rewritten to say that, and to state what the price does imply: 0.82x book against our 0.46x target [S0] [S3].

challenges.challenge: The RNAV leg (60% weight) contains no land valuation. params.landbank_basis says landbank_value equals total assets 3,693.5 less cash 188.8 less the recurring business 202.9, which is Rp3,301.8bn, but the input is Rp2,921.0bn - a Rp380.8bn (13%) gap with no explanation. The value chosen makes RNAV exactly parent book: rnav_per_share 493.18 versus parent BVPS 491.27 at 30 Sep 2026 (0.4%). The asset leg is therefore book x0.6 and the P/BV leg is the same book x0.916; their 296-versus-450 divergence is the discount choice, not independent evidence, and the house card requirement of land at appraised or market value with a stated land-bank haircut is unmet.
challenges.answer: params.landbank_basis now reproduces the input line by line: total assets 3,693.45 less cash 188.81 less non-debt liabilities 389.56 less the capitalised recurring business 194.09 equals 2,921.0, all at 30 September 2026. Section 4 states that adding the recurring stream back and deducting net debt and minorities makes RNAV an identity equal to parent book, that the 0.4% gap is exactly the 194 versus 203 capitalisation difference, and that no appraisal exists [S0] [S3].

challenges.challenge: Rp59.3bn, 15.4% of FY2025 revenue, is dropped from the revenue build: dev_revenue 260.40 plus recurring_revenue 66.64 = 327.04 against a revenue line of 386.08, with hotel 52.52, strata 3.81 and rent 2.94 (F4-F6, quoted but unused) sitting outside. FY2026E 408.49 is built off the smaller base, so the 30.0% growth in section 3 is +5.8% on the reported total and implies Q4-2026 revenue 31% below Q4-2025 after 9M +40%. At the 50% recurring margin the omitted gross profit is about Rp29.6bn, roughly half of FY2026E EBITDA of 58.6bn.
challenges.answer: Section 3 no longer calls the year a recovery: FY2026E revenue growth is now shown with the model's own like-for-like figure against the reported total, the three omitted segments are named with their F4/F5/F6 values, and the omitted gross profit is stated at the recurring margin as a material share of modelled EBITDA. We did not model the three segments because the template carries one development and one recurring line and we hold no sourced combined total to key a fact to [S9] [S0].

challenges.challenge: The stated rationale for the 40% RNAV discount contradicts the haircut actually applied. Section 4 calls 40% the narrow end of the band because the RNAV is already unmarked and a second full illiquidity discount would double count, and the engine then removes 30% for liquidity, taking the effective discount to 58% and the target to 0.42x book. Meanwhile 0.40 is below what this book applies to peers (LPCK 0.55, CTRA 0.55, SMRA 0.60, BSDE 0.65, LPKR 0.71, PWON 0.72, median near 0.55).
challenges.answer: The double-count argument is deleted. Section 4 now states the effective discount actually applied — the RNAV discount compounded with the liquidity haircut, roughly two-fifths of RNAV on the asset leg — and shows the target against book value per share at under half of book, below the peer range, with the control price as the only anchor [S0] [S3].

challenges.challenge: The 15% free-float deadline of 31 March 2029 (F34, S15) is modelled only as a dilution risk. The mirror case is not considered: BSDE can meet the rule by taking SMDM private, and buying the 1.03% float (~48.7m shares) at Rp402 costs about Rp19.6bn, which is 1.6% of the Rp1,196bn it paid for control. An IDX delisting buyback requires an independent appraisal, i.e. exactly the appraisal the report says would change its mind, and the deadline gives it a date. The bull scenario is only +12% (353) and contains none of this.
challenges.answer: The buyout route is now in the bull narrative and in section 5: with the float at 1.02% a buyout at an appraised price would cost BSDE a fraction of the Rp1,196.4bn it paid for control, and a delisting buyback would force the independent appraisal. It does not change the rating: at full RNAV before any discount the asset leg still sits below the traded price after the haircut [S15] [S3].

challenges.challenge: No land value is ever estimated. Rancamaya land for development is 1,355,548 sqm carried at Rp576.4bn (F24/F25), or Rp425,000 per sqm, and ready-for-sale Rancamaya inventory is Rp1,105.7bn (F26), yet the report only asserts that carrying cost is far below Bogor market land values. The bull case re-rates the RNAV discount from 40% to 30% but still multiplies book, so the land thesis is never quantified: a sourced Rp1.0m per sqm on Rancamaya alone adds Rp779bn to the landbank, about Rp98 per share to the RNAV leg and roughly 21% to the target.
challenges.answer: We state that no sourced uplift exists: no Bogor corridor benchmark, NJOP schedule or appraisal could be obtained, and the assumption file now records the carrying cost per sqm of Rancamaya land and says the asset case rests on book. The one arm's-length whole-company price, BSDE's 2025 purchase, was struck below book, so the sourced evidence points to a discount, not an uplift [S3] [S0].

challenges.challenge: Related-party gravity is asserted but neither sourced nor priced: the claim that the controlling shareholder is also the main contractor, infrastructure provider and potentially the buyer of land carries no citation, and the report then says that disclosures do not allow related-party flows to be quantified as a share of revenue. EARNINGS_QUALITY_FLAGS item 4 requires that percentage, and a controller who can buy the land bank at cost is the most direct route to permanent RNAV loss - it appears in no scenario.
challenges.answer: The contractor, infrastructure and land-buyer assertion is withdrawn as unsourced, and the related-party share of revenue is recorded as not verified rather than as zero: BSDE's consolidated related-party balances are not SMDM's. Section 5 adds why it does not move the value: the base case already prices the whole land bank at cost and never credits a market uplift, so leakage at cost cannot erode an RNAV that assumed none [S3] [S0].

challenges.challenge: The actual IDX board and notation status of SMDM is never established and the HSC argument is inferential: sections 2 and 6 say the ownership profile is exactly the shape the regime is aimed at, but neither S13 nor S14 names SMDM in the 383-name list and no source states its board. EARNINGS_QUALITY_FLAGS item 3 says to check this first, because a special-monitoring board with full call auction breaks every entry and exit assumption, and it underpins the 30% liquidity haircut and the investability of a SELL.
challenges.answer: Sections 2 and 6 no longer imply SMDM is on the HSC list: the published list does not name it, and we hold no source for its board or notation status, which is now recorded as unverified. The liquidity haircut is restated as resting on the Rp30.6m ADTV and the 1.02% float, not on a board designation, and the status is added to the monitoring list [S14] [S0].

challenges.challenge: Section 6 asserts there is no restatement, no going-concern notation and no evidence of manipulation-class flags, although the analyst states the company LK and annual report could not be obtained. Absence of evidence from a Yahoo statement dump is not evidence of a clean audit opinion, and the same paragraph claim that negative operating cash flow is explained by inventory skips the numbers: inventory rose 17.3% (762.7 to 894.9) while COGS fell 51.7%, inventory now equals 2.3x revenue, and operating cash flow was negative in both FY2024A (-88.4) and FY2025A (-134.8).
challenges.answer: The clean-audit claim is downgraded to not verified, with the reason stated: we could not obtain SMDM's annual report or opinion. Sections 3 and 6 now report the earnings-quality evidence from the numbers: negative operating cash flow in both years against positive profit, an accruals ratio in low single digits, and inventory rising while cost of revenue fell, with the cost-of-revenue values quoted from the model [S0].

challenges.challenge: The price history the thesis turns on is omitted. The pack records a 52-week range of Rp368-Rp1,260 against Rp402 today: the shares are 68% below the high (Rp6.0tn market value at Rp1,260 versus Rp1.92tn now) and 9% above the low, on a float worth about Rp19.6bn. The report framing - a scarcity price carrying a large premium that should drift back toward asset value - reads as though the premium is fresh, when most of the de-rating has already happened. That is material both to the -44% expected return and to the house card requirement of a named, dated catalyst.
challenges.answer: The investment summary now carries the twelve-month trading range and market value from the pack, says most of the de-rating has already happened, and names the dated events that would close the remaining gap: the FY2026 annual report, the VAT lapse and the free-float deadline. The premium argument no longer reads as if it were fresh [S0] [S15] [S11].

challenges.challenge: Source and figure hygiene: (a) S7 is registered as the SMDM offeree circular for the 2025 BSDE tender offer but the archived document is the Sinarmas Land SGX circular for the Lyon Investments voluntary cash offer, and it is cited nowhere; (b) F1 labels 260.40 as presales although it comes from the same sentence as F2 dev_revenue and the report thesis is that no presales KPI exists; (c) sections 2 and 5 say BI held at 5.8% while S10 and F33 say 5.75%; (d) the extreme_call note says Rp30.6bn ADTV where the pack is Rp30,551,448 and section 4 says Rp30.6m; (e) F32 shows 10,043 in the COMMERCIAL row of the BSDE presales table (Residential 4,190, Others 2,127), so group marketing sales of 10,043 is a segment figure; (f) rendered units read 1,989 year, 2,027 year, 383 count and 4,390 m shares.
challenges.answer: S7 is deleted from the source registry because the archived document is the Sinarmas Land SGX circular, not the SMDM offeree circular, and it was cited nowhere. F1 is relabelled as development revenue with the presales-proxy role stated, the ADTV is stated as Rp30.6m in the extreme_call justification, F32 is rendered in trillions, and the policy rate renders from F33 at 5.75% throughout [S9] [S10] [S8].

challenges.challenge: cap_rate 0.18 applied to recurring gross profit is 1.8x the industry book median of about 0.10 (range 0.055-0.21). The bridge in the report (a 9% NOI cap over a 50% NOI-to-gross-profit ratio) is coherent in itself, but it values the hotel and estate assets at Rp203bn where a 0.10 rate gives Rp350bn - Rp147bn of RNAV, roughly Rp11 per share on the target. Nothing in the sources says the SMDM hotel and estate services deserve a 9% NOI cap while peers are at 8-10% on gross profit.
challenges.answer: params.cap_rate_basis now reconciles the rate: the engine capitalises recurring gross profit, so 0.18 on gross profit is a 9% NOI cap given a 50% recurring margin and roughly half of that margin taken by property opex. The 0.10 default applied to gross profit implies a 5% NOI yield, which is prime-CBD pricing, and the basis states the value it would produce and that it would not close the gap to the price [S9] [S3].

challenges.challenge: Summary renders market capitalisation as IDR1,918,399,571.27tn because fund record line 67 formats mkt.mcap_idr (Rp1,918,399,571,274 in full IDR) with |idrtn, which assumes an IDR-bn input and divides by 1e3.
challenges.answer: Summary market value now renders mkt.mcap_idr with |idrb (IDR1,918.4bn) instead of |idrtn, which divided a full-IDR pack value by 1e3; it was the only mcap_idr use in the file [S0].

challenges.challenge: Section 1 says SMDM 'was, until the 2025 takeover, controlled by the Widjaja family through Top Global Limited'; no source in the file ties TGL to that family and S3 p.155 describes TGL as a third party to BSDE, so the sentence contradicts our own source.
challenges.answer: Removed the unsourced Widjaja attribution; the text now says only that Top Global Limited controlled SMDM until the 2025 takeover and that the filing treats it as a third party to BSDE, then gives BSDE's stake [S3].

challenges.challenge: Section 3 pairs FY2027E revenue with FY2026E EBITDA and FY2030E revenue with FY2027E EBITDA: 58.6 and 72.7 are FY2026E and FY2027E, while FY2030E EBITDA is 103.6.
challenges.answer: EBITDA pair corrected: the FY2027E revenue now pairs with fin.FY2027E.ebitda and FY2030E revenue with fin.FY2030E.ebitda, both placeholders, so the text cannot drift from the model again [S9].

challenges.challenge: Section 5 says the bear takes development growth down by 30.0%; the applied shock is -0.10 on presales_growth (30% to 20%) and -0.10 on recurring margin, i.e. ten points, so the text overstates the bear severity threefold.
challenges.answer: Bear description now reads ten percentage points off the base growth path, recurring gross margin off ten points and RNAV discount widened ten points, exactly the three add shocks in fund record [S0].

challenges.challenge: Section 4 says the Rp224 target is 'below the range at which this desk carries the listed developer peer set'; our own models carry LPCK at 0.34x and LPKR at 0.24x book, both below SMDM's 0.46x, so the claim is contradicted by the peer set it invokes.
challenges.answer: Deleted the peer-range claim; the text now states the target is under half of book and says explicitly that LPCK and LPKR are also carried well below book on this desk's models, so the case rests on the control price [S3].

missing_bull_case.note: Two absent. First, the 31 Mar 2029 float deadline is modelled only as dilution; the mirror is a delisting or tender buyout of the 1.03% float (~48.7m shares, ~Rp19.6bn at Rp402, 1.6% of the Rp1,196bn BSDE paid), which under IDX rules requires an independent appraisal - the very appraisal the report says would change its mind. Second, no land-value work at all: Rancamaya is 1,355,548 sqm carried at Rp576.4bn (Rp425k/sqm, F24/F25) and the report asserts this is far below Bogor market land values without quantifying a sourced comparable, so even the bull (RNAV discount 30%) values book, not land.

missing_bear_case.note: Cyclical, VAT-cliff, free-float-dilution and liquidity risks are covered well. Missing: related-party gravity is asserted (main contractor, infrastructure provider and potentially buyer of land) with no source and no value in the bear case, although EARNINGS_QUALITY_FLAGS item 4 makes it the modal channel; and the IDX board and notation status and HSC-list membership of SMDM are never established, so the exit assumption is unverified.

assumption_realism.note: Dev growth of 30% is the highest in the industry book and recog_current=1.0 avoids a lag haircut, both defensible on the 9M run-rate; opex held flat is properly justified. Not realistic: dev 260.40 plus recurring 66.64 = 327.04 against a revenue line of 386.08, so FY2026E is built off a base 15.4% below the last actual; and cap_rate 0.18 is 1.8x the peer median.

evidence_and_citations.note: Most load-bearing figures verify in the archive (S3 notes 35 and inventory, S9 segment revenue and profit, S13 383 names, S15 15% float, S16 400ha and 1989). Failing: S7 is Sinarmas Land SGX circular for the Lyon Investments offer, not an SMDM offeree circular, and is uncited; F1 labels 260.40 as presales although it comes from the same sentence as F2 dev_revenue and no presales KPI exists; S10 says 5.75% but the prose says 5.8% twice; the extreme_call note says Rp30.6bn ADTV where the pack is Rp30.55m; and no going-concern notation is asserted without the LK.

valuation_method_fit.note: COC inputs are clean (rf 7.45%, ERP 4.23%, CRP 2.46%, beta 0.9, WACC 11.85%) and the minority and net-debt bridge in RNAV is right. But the primary method is not a land RNAV: the stated landbank basis (3,693.5 less 188.8 less 202.9) gives 3,301.8 against an input of 2,921.0, and the resulting RNAV pre-discount of Rp493.18 per share equals parent BVPS of Rp491.27 to 0.4%, so the 60% leg is book x0.6 and the P/BV leg is the same book x0.916. No cross-check is independent and the method card requirement of appraised land with a stated haircut is unmet.

bias_and_tone.note: The prose overstates what the model does: section 4 says development gross margin, cap rate and terminal growth dominate the sensitivity when the grid varies only presales growth (zero effect) and RNAV discount; section 5 says the bear takes growth down by 30.0% against a -10pp shock. The 52-week range (Rp368-Rp1,260, i.e. 68% below the high and 9% above the low) is never disclosed, so the reader cannot see how much of the de-rating has already happened.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: Deck variables read correctly: BI path of 5.75% matches the macro deck bi_rate 5.75 and F33; the INDO rate-sensitive AVOID tilt is consistent with a SELL on a mortgage-dependent developer; rnav_discount 0.40 sits inside the industry book range of 0.00-0.86 (median ~0.55) and the 10% tax is the LK effective rate. The one exception is cap_rate 0.18 against peers at 0.08-0.16, raised separately.

conservatism_audit.note: Stacked conservatism that moves the rating: (a) Rp59.3bn of FY2025 revenue (hotel 52.52, strata 3.81, rent 2.94) is outside the build, ~Rp29.6bn of gross profit and about half of FY2026E EBITDA, with no offsetting source; (b) cap_rate 0.18 against a peer median near 0.10 costs ~Rp147bn of RNAV; (c) the 40% RNAV discount is justified as the narrow end because a second illiquidity discount would double count, and a 30% haircut is then applied anyway (58% combined). Credit: no default volume haircut, payout nil consistent with history, no invented appraisal.

calibration.note: The 2.49pp FY2025A EBITDA-margin gap (actual 11.86% vs model 14.34%) is unexplained in qc_justifications and is a denominator artefact: 45.77/327.04 = 14.0%, because the model revenue components omit Rp59.3bn that the reported line includes. The extreme_call BLOCK is cleared with a claim that the report contains a reverse DCF; fund record records reverse_dcf available=false and price not bracketed, and section 4 has none. drift.opex_pct is properly justified.

signoff.notes: Second sign-off, after the round-one return was answered. The five FIX items that blocked the first pass are closed on the page: market cap renders IDR1,918.4bn, the control attribution no longer names an unsourced family, the EBITDA years pair with their own revenue, the bear is described as the applied ten-point shocks, and the peer-range claim is deleted and replaced by the LPCK/LPKR disclosure. check --run passes (facts PASS, lint PASS, engine QC no blockers) and the engine rerun reproduces SELL, Rp224, -44.2%. On the substance: the rating is the most likely path, not the most cautious one - the RNAV is struck at carrying value with no land uplift, the report says plainly that no appraisal exists and that RNAV equals parent book by construction, the discount and the liquidity haircut compound to roughly two-fifths of RNAV, and the bull case now carries the buyout route so the float/15% rule is not read one way only. Scenarios are mirrored (presales_growth, recurring margin and the RNAV discount all shocked by ten points each way, 50/25/25). The card's RNAV-with-explicit-haircut method is used with evidenced inputs (Rancamaya 1,355,548 sqm at Rp576.4bn, inventory lines, the Rp1,196.4bn control price), the recurring-income share and net cash position are stated, and every factual paragraph carries its source. The three open NOTEs do not change the rating or target and none is a reader-facing error in the note: (Q9) the drift.opex_pct justification says flat in nominal terms while the model carries Rp204.2bn to Rp286.1bn, which is flat in real terms - wording, and the model's real-flat cost is the defensible one; (Q10) the recurring bucket capitalises the other-segments line and not the hotel stream, but the hotel's assets sit inside the landbank residual at carrying value, so capitalising its income as well would risk double counting, and the report states the revenue-build omission and its direction; (Q11) the 14.3% model against 11.9% actual EBITDA margin is the same narrower-revenue-base effect that section 3 now states explicitly as a like-for-like reading, so the gap is named where it is created. Fix Q9's wording at the next refresh; a second return would park a well-evidenced SELL over wording and I do not think that is warranted.

bias.note: Base case is anchored, not cautious: FY2026E revenue Rp408.5bn sits 5.8% above FY2025A on the narrower build, opex Rp202.9bn is held at the last actual in real terms [S0], FY2025A EBITDA Rp45.8bn recomputes from the filing, RNAV is struck at carrying value with no uplift, the 40% RNAV discount is the narrow end of the house band and the 30% haircut is the house illiquidity schedule on Rp30.6m ADTV. Every drift is sourced; the only unsourced directions (hotel/strata/rent omitted from the build, hotel stream outside the recurring bucket) are disclosed as conservative and do not reach the target because no valuation leg reads the forecast [S9, S3]. Scenarios are mirrored (presales +/-10pp, recurring margin +/-10pp, RNAV discount +/-10pp) with base 50%, bear/bull 25/25 [S15]. Round-1 Q1-Q8 verified closed in the text, not merely reworded.

findings.finding: qc_justifications drift.opex_pct describes opex as held flat in nominal absolute terms at about Rp203bn, but fund record carries it from Rp204.2bn in FY2026E to Rp286.1bn in FY2035E, i.e. flat in real terms at about 3.8%/yr. The economics are right and match the house standard; only the wording is wrong.

The recurring bucket is the other-segments line of Rp66.6bn (F3) and excludes hotel Rp52.5bn (F4), so the capitalised recurring business omits the hotel stream worth roughly Rp146bn at the 50% margin / 18% cap rate, about Rp31/share of pre-discount RNAV. Section 3 quantifies the EBITDA gap but not this asset-side gap.

Calibration shows model FY2025A-basis EBITDA margin 14.3% against actual 11.9% (2.5pp). Section 3 explains it as fixed-cost leverage on a recovering top line, which is the sourced opex story, but the gap is not named in the report.

flags.message: a.opex_pct moves -6.0pp from FY2026E to FY2035E: source the change or hold it
flags.justification: Opex is held flat in nominal absolute terms at about Rp203bn (FY2025A gross profit Rp242.88bn less EBIT Rp39.96bn, [S0]) while revenue recovers from the collapsed FY2025 base of Rp386.08bn [S9]: the ratio therefore falls 6pp. That is fixed-cost leverage on an existing estate, not an assumption of margin expansion, and no new cost line is introduced.

flags.message: expected return -44%: name the two or three sourced drivers that produce it and what today's price implies (reverse DCF)
flags.justification: Three sourced drivers produce the deeply negative expected return. First, the RNAV is struck at carrying value with no appraisal uplift, and at carrying value it is an identity that returns parent book value per share: Rancamaya land for development Rp576.4bn for 1,355,548 sqm (F24, F25) and ready-for-sale Rancamaya inventory Rp1,105.7bn (F26). Second, the asset leg loses a 40% RNAV discount and then a further 30% liquidity haircut for a Rp30.6m ADTV on a 1.02% free float [S0], an effective 58% off book. Third, the only arm's-length whole-company price is BSDE's 2025 purchase of 91.99% for Rp1,196.4bn (F22, F23), about Rp272 a share, below book. What the price implies is NOT a growth rate: the engine's reverse test on a.presales_growth returns available=false with "price not bracketed" because the RNAV leg does not contain growth and the earnings and book legs are struck off reported LTM earnings and current equity, so no presales growth in the tested range (-50% to +50% on the shock axis) reaches Rp402 — that invariance is itself the finding, and is stated as such in section 4 rather than papered over. The price instead implies an appraisal uplift above book value, which we could not source, or the removal of the RNAV discount, which would still leave the target below the price after the liquidity haircut.
